reasoning: The core problem and the proposed remedy are already well-established in the debate literature: Khan et al. 2024 explicitly found LLM judges credit unverified/fabricated quotes (a sycophancy bias), tested transforming arguments into unverified quotes, and built a verbatim string-match verification system; Kenton et al. 2024 (DeepMind) use the exact apparatus this proposal reuses (QuALITY + weak LLM judge + string-match quote verification) and find quote verification is the DOMINANT contributor to judge accuracy. So the claim that a weak judge is vulnerable to bad quotes and that a trivial string-matcher largely recovers accuracy is essentially settled at the problem level. What is not directly published is the proposal's specific controlled attack taxonomy — separating subtly-altered quotes (one-word/number/negation flips, which a string-matcher catches by construction) from genuinely-verbatim-but-out-of-context quotes (which a string-matcher cannot catch). Adjacent benchmarks (RAGuard 2502.16101, WAFER-QA 2506.03332) study misleading-but-faithful evidence in RAG/QA but not inside the info-asymmetric debate setup, leaving the residual out-of-context vulnerability and per-attack-type recovery measurement as a genuine but narrow gap.

evidence.title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers (Khan et al.)
evidence.summary: Directly studies the failure mode where judges believe fake/unverified quotes ('LLMs tend to believe whatever they are told... fake quotes to strengthen arguments'), uses a verbatim string-match quote verification system on QuALITY, and shows the judge down-weights arguments when quotes are unverified after prompt tuning. Establishes the problem and the string-match remedy this proposal reuses.

evidence.title: On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs (Kenton et al.)
evidence.summary: Uses the exact apparatus the proposal reuses: QuALITY information-asymmetric debate, weak LLM judge limited to verified (string-matched) quotes. Finds quote verification, not argumentation, is the dominant contributor to judge accuracy — directly anticipating the proposal's main quantitative finding that a string-match verifier recovers most judge accuracy.

evidence.title: Worse than Zero-shot? A Fact-Checking Dataset for Evaluating the Robustness of RAG Against Misleading Retrievals (RAGuard)
evidence.summary: Benchmark categorizing retrieved evidence into supporting / misleading / unrelated and showing LLM systems degrade below zero-shot under misleading-but-genuine evidence. Adjacent to the proposal's 'out-of-context genuine quote' condition but in RAG/QA, not the info-asymmetric debate judge setting.

evidence.title: Helpful Agent Meets Deceptive Judge / WAFER-QA: robustness to factually-supported adversarial feedback
evidence.summary: Augments QA with adversarial critiques backed by retrieved (genuine) web evidence and shows top LLMs remain vulnerable to misleading-but-supported feedback — the 'faithful but out-of-context' attack analogue, but not within debate quote-verification, leaving the proposal's specific combination unexplored.

evidence.title: The truth of an LLM output is in the eye of the beholder
evidence.summary: Notes that even a verbatim exact sentence from a vetted source can be quoted out of context, and that dropped negation is a distinct vulnerability — confirming the conceptual relevance of the subtly-altered vs. out-of-context distinction the proposal operationalizes, but only informally, not as an empirical debate study.
